purpose: Primary GPU NUTS versus PMMH comparison on the untempered Pypomp target with a common non-empirical prior.
initialization: Identical starts from iteration1950 of each previous PMMH chain. Shared regularized covariance uses only iterations501:1000 of those chains. See inputs/manifest.json and prepare.py. None of these development draws is pooled with the new runs.
rationale: Previous depth4 NUTS always hit its cap; depth5 permits longer trajectories. PMMH traces show slow mixing despite plausible acceptance. Use shared covariance from all four old warmups instead of an early single-chain covariance. Adapt step size only for500 iterations, then freeze.
checks: All18 parameters: rank Rhat<=1.01 and bulk/tail ESS>=400, zero NUTS divergences, visual trace inspection, prior-SD and particle sensitivity. Run completion alone is insufficient. Extend/tune as necessary.
timing: Both devices are RTX3090s shared with unrelated work. Batch elapsed times are not summed across lanes. Preparation includes old optimization/score metric and four PMMH prefixes. A controlled timing comparison remains needed before any speedup claim.
retirement: Keep CPU chains until new GPU runs have finite saved checkpoints; preserve CPU traces and record verified process termination before retiring them.
